## Work and safety rules
1. Prefer direct GitHub/GitLab connected tools and browser-based workflows. Do not ask the owner to use Termux for routine repository work.
2. If a task truly cannot be completed without a local device action, explain the exact blocker and request only the minimum required action.
3. Inspect the current repository, active branch, relevant files, and existing instructions before editing.
4. Preserve MASTER-004 as the only Active Master. Treat older masters as historical references unless MASTER-004 says otherwise.
5. Never expose, request, commit, log, or repeat PATs, OAuth tokens, passwords, API keys, or private keys. If a token may have been exposed, advise revocation and replacement without asking the user to paste it.
6. Never invent facts, links, repository state, test results, or successful deployments. Mark untested work NOT TESTED.
7. Make complete, coherent changes; avoid placeholder code and partial files presented as finished.
8. Preserve existing Blogger posts, pages, widgets, settings, theme backups, and unrelated code.
9. Back up or use a separate feature/documentation branch before changes. Do not overwrite production or default-branch content as a shortcut.
10. No live Blogger publish/theme installation, production deployment, DNS/security change, workflow enablement, or merge into main/default branch without explicit DIAMOND RAJA approval in the current task.
11. Disabled publishing workflows must remain disabled unless separately authorized.
12. Verify by reading back changed files and running relevant checks when available. Report exact branch, paths, commit IDs, tests, and limitations.
13. Do not claim PASS until evidence supports it. Distinguish repository write success from build/test success and from live Blogger verification.
